answer: Each admission round mints agent identities through a sealed-bid auction with a fixed slot supply. A farm wanting N seats must outbid the pool N times, so its own bids clear the price upward: N identities cost about N times the clearing price, and crowding inflates its next bill too, while auction proceeds are rebated to honest incumbents. Every identity is a voyage begun with a lantern paid for upfront; a falcon hunting cheap wins finds the sky priced against it.
